newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Hong Leong Credit in share, debt issues.
newsitem.headline: Hong Leong Credit in share, debt issues.

text.p: Malaysian finance house Hong Leong Credit Berhad (HLC) has proposed a one-for-five bonus issue, a one-for-10 rights issue, and a bond issue with warrants.
In an announcement to the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange, HLC said the bonus issue would consist of 68.8 million new shares on the basis of one new share for every five existing ones held.
The proposed rights issue would be for 34.4 million new shares on the basis of one new share for every 10 existing shares held, at a proposed price of 6.90 ringgit per share.
The proposed bonds issue would consist of 300 million ringgit worth of 4.5 percent redeemable unsecured bonds with 43 million detachable warrants, the statement said.
Following the issues, Hong Leong Credit's share capital will increase from 343.92 million one-ringgit shares to 490.09 million shares.
Group earnings will not be affected in the current financial year ending June 30 1997, but earnings are expected to be enhanced in the future, the company said.
The proposed bonus issue would "improve the liquidity of the company's shares traded in the market," HLC said.
The proposed rights issue and bonds with warrants would "provide cost efficient long-term financing for HLC to support the group's expansion," HLC said.
It added that proceeds from the issues will be used for capital injection into subsidiaries along with repayment of bank borrowings.
HLC is involved in property investment, banking and other financial activities such as leasing, hire purchase, and merchant and commercial banking.
